question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
In geography class, / the teacher told the students, / "Switzerland lies / inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy."
option_1: inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy" contains the error. Switzerland does not lie inside these four countries; it is a separate, independent country that shares its borders with (is surrounded by) Germany, France, Austria, and Italy (and Liechtenstein).

• Rule — Correct preposition of position: When one place is bordered by, or located amid, several other places (without being a part of them), the correct preposition is "amid", "among", or the phrase "surrounded by", not "inside". "Inside" means located within the boundary of something, i.e., as a part of it.

• Corrected segment: Switzerland lies amid / is surrounded by Germany, France, Austria, and Italy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "In geography class," is grammatically and factually correct; it correctly introduces the setting of the sentence.

• Option 3: "Switzerland lies" is grammatically correct — the singular subject "Switzerland" correctly takes the singular verb "lies".

• Option 4: "the teacher told the students," is grammatically correct — subject-verb agreement and the reporting structure are both fine.

NOTE

• Such "spot the error" questions sometimes test preposition/word-choice accuracy together with grammar — always check whether the chosen word logically and correctly conveys the intended meaning, not just whether the sentence is syntactically well-formed.

• Common confusing prepositions of position: "between" (for two), "among" (for more than two), "amid" (in the middle of, surrounded by), "inside" (within the boundary of).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
There are eight planets in our solar system and a Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
option_3: and a Earth is the third
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. and a Earth is the third

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "and a Earth is the third" contains the error. "Earth" is a proper noun (the name of our planet), and proper nouns do not take the indefinite article "a/an" before them.

• Rule — Articles with proper nouns: The indefinite articles "a" and "an" are used only before common, countable nouns in the singular. Proper nouns (names of specific people, places, planets, etc.) are normally used without any article.

• Corrected segment: "and Earth is the third".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "planet from the Sun." is correct — it needs no article and correctly completes the sentence.

• Option 2: "in our solar system" is correct — the possessive determiner "our" is correctly used before "solar system".

• Option 4: "There are eight planets" is correct — the plural subject "planets" correctly takes the plural verb "are".

NOTE

• Other proper nouns commonly tested without an article in SSC exams: names of planets (Mars, Venus), continents, most countries, and people's names — e.g., "Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun" (not "a Mars").

• Exception: an article IS used with a proper noun when it is qualified by an adjective, e.g., "the young Einstein was fascinated by science."

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
‘You expressed your opinion/ very clearly /but I am sorry/ I cannot agree to you’.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I cannot agree to you

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "I cannot agree to you" contains the error. When we agree with a person, the correct preposition is "with", not "to".

• Rule — Preposition after "agree":
◦ Agree with + person (I agree with him.)
◦ Agree to + proposal/suggestion/plan (I agree to your proposal.)
◦ Agree on + a matter under discussion (We agreed on the price.)

• Corrected segment: "I cannot agree with you".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "You expressed your opinion" is grammatically correct.

• Option 2: "very clearly" is a correctly formed adverbial phrase modifying "expressed".

• Option 4: "but I am sorry" is grammatically correct; the conjunction "but" correctly introduces the contrasting clause.

NOTE

• Commonly confused prepositions after verbs in SSC exams: agree with/to/on, married to, good at, afraid of, angry with (a person)/at (a thing), depend on.

• Remember: we "agree to" a thing (plan, suggestion, proposal) but "agree with" a person (or an idea/opinion of a person).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Serena _________ from fever since the 5th of this month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has been suffering

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the time marker "since the 5th of this month", which indicates an action that started in the past and is still continuing up to the present moment.

• Rule — Present Perfect Continuous Tense:
◦ Structure: Subject + has/have + been + V-ing + since/for + time
◦ "Since" is used with a point of time (since 5 o'clock, since Monday, since the 5th of this month) and "for" is used with a period/duration of time (for two days).

• Applying the rule: Serena (third person singular) + has been + suffering (V-ing) + since the 5th of this month.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "is suffering" (Present Continuous) is incorrect — it does not show that the action began in the past and has continued till now; it is used for an action happening right now or a fixed future arrangement.

• Option 3: "suffers" (Simple Present) is incorrect — it indicates a habitual/general action, not a continuing action linked to a specific past starting point.

• Option 4: "suffered" (Simple Past) is incorrect — it indicates a completed action in the past, but the sentence with "since" clearly indicates the action is still ongoing.

NOTE

• "Since" always pairs with a perfect tense (present perfect / present perfect continuous), never with the simple present or simple past.

• Other examples: "I have been living here since 2015." "She has been waiting since morning."

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The disclaimer read that no animals were harmed (1)________ the filming of that scene. However, they forgot that the brand of lipstick that was applied (2)________ the heroines lips for that scene was manufactured from crushed cochineal bugs, which release a pigment commonly used in red lipstick. The other items in the film studio (3)________ used animal fats during their manufacturing. The actors who (4)________ that they are vegan in past interviews are unaware of their indirect involvement in such acts of cruelty against animals. The indirect cruelty against animals does not stop here. For example, the extensive disposal of plastic waste in oceans has made plastic a part of the animal food chain, which is detrimental (5)________ our entire ecosystem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. during.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a preposition of time that connects an action/event ("no animals were harmed") with a period/event during which it took place ("the filming of that scene"). "During" is the correct choice as it means "throughout the course of" / "at some point in the course of" a specified period or event.

• Rule: "During" is followed by a noun/noun phrase denoting a period of time or an event (during the meeting, during the film, during the war), whereas "while" is followed by a clause (subject + verb).

• Applying the rule: no animals were harmed during the filming (noun phrase) of that scene.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "around" is incorrect; "around" indicates approximate time or physical surrounding, not the time-span of an ongoing event.

• Option 3: "from" is incorrect; "from" indicates a starting point, and would need a corresponding "to/till" to indicate a duration, which is missing here.

• Option 4: "for" is incorrect; "for" is used to indicate a duration/length of time expressed in numbers (for two hours, for a week), not to link an action to an event taking place.

NOTE

• Commonly confused time prepositions in SSC: "during" (course of an event/noun) vs. "while" (course of an action/clause) vs. "for" (length of time) vs. "since" (point of starting time).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The disclaimer read that no animals were harmed (1)________ the filming of that scene. However, they forgot that the brand of lipstick that was applied (2)________ the heroines lips for that scene was manufactured from crushed cochineal bugs, which release a pigment commonly used in red lipstick. The other items in the film studio (3)________ used animal fats during their manufacturing. The actors who (4)________ that they are vegan in past interviews are unaware of their indirect involvement in such acts of cruelty against animals. The indirect cruelty against animals does not stop here. For example, the extensive disposal of plastic waste in oceans has made plastic a part of the animal food chain, which is detrimental (5)________ our entire ecosystem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires the preposition that correctly follows the verb "applied" when something is put onto a surface. The correct collocation is "apply something to something".

• Rule — Fixed preposition with "apply": "Apply to" is used when a substance is put on/onto a surface (apply cream to the skin, apply lipstick to the lips) or when making a request (apply to a college).

• Applying the rule: the lipstick that was applied to the heroine's lips.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "on" is incorrect; while colloquially possible, the standard tested collocation with the verb "apply" is "apply to", not "apply on".

• Option 3: "over" is incorrect; "over" suggests covering something from above, which does not fit the fixed verb-preposition collocation being tested here.

• Option 4: "upon" is incorrect for the same reason as "on" — it does not match the standard collocation "apply...to".

NOTE

• Other fixed verb + preposition combinations frequently tested in SSC: apply for (a job), apply to (a surface/institution), depend on, insist on, rely on.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The disclaimer read that no animals were harmed (1)________ the filming of that scene. However, they forgot that the brand of lipstick that was applied (2)________ the heroines lips for that scene was manufactured from crushed cochineal bugs, which release a pigment commonly used in red lipstick. The other items in the film studio (3)________ used animal fats during their manufacturing. The actors who (4)________ that they are vegan in past interviews are unaware of their indirect involvement in such acts of cruelty against animals. The indirect cruelty against animals does not stop here. For example, the extensive disposal of plastic waste in oceans has made plastic a part of the animal food chain, which is detrimental (5)________ our entire ecosystem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. also.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that logically links the new information (other items in the studio also used animal fats) to the previous sentence (the lipstick was made using crushed cochineal bugs). "Also" correctly conveys the idea of addition — that, in addition to the lipstick, other studio items too involved animal-derived substances.

• Rule — Additive connectors: Words like "also," "too," "as well," "in addition" are used to add a similar point to what has already been stated. "Also" is typically placed before the main verb in a sentence.

• Applying the rule: The other items in the film studio also used animal fats during their manufacturing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "long" is incorrect; it is an adjective/adverb of duration or degree and does not fit the sense of addition required here.

• Option 3: "least" is incorrect; "least" indicates the smallest amount/degree, which contradicts the intended meaning of the sentence.

• Option 4: "too" is incorrect here only because of position — "too" conveys the same additive meaning as "also" but is normally placed at the end of a clause/sentence, not before the verb as required by this blank's position in the sentence.

NOTE

• Placement rule: "also" — usually mid-sentence, before the main verb; "too" and "as well" — usually at the end of the sentence/clause.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The disclaimer read that no animals were harmed (1)________ the filming of that scene. However, they forgot that the brand of lipstick that was applied (2)________ the heroines lips for that scene was manufactured from crushed cochineal bugs, which release a pigment commonly used in red lipstick. The other items in the film studio (3)________ used animal fats during their manufacturing. The actors who (4)________ that they are vegan in past interviews are unaware of their indirect involvement in such acts of cruelty against animals. The indirect cruelty against animals does not stop here. For example, the extensive disposal of plastic waste in oceans has made plastic a part of the animal food chain, which is detrimental (5)________ our entire ecosystem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. confessed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "in past interviews" clearly places the action of confessing being vegan at a definite point of time in the past, which requires the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense: Used for an action that started and finished at a specific, definite time in the past, and is often identified by expressions such as "in [past interviews/year]," "yesterday," "last week."

• Applying the rule: The actors who confessed (V2, simple past) that they are vegan in past interviews.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "were confessing" (Past Continuous) is incorrect; it would suggest an ongoing action interrupted by another past action, which is not the intended meaning.

• Option 2: "had confessed" (Past Perfect) is incorrect; the past perfect is used for an action completed before another past action, but no such second past action is indicated here.

• Option 4: "are confessing" (Present Continuous) is incorrect; it wrongly places the action in the present, contradicting the time marker "in past interviews."

NOTE

• Whenever a sentence carries a definite past time marker (in [past year/event], yesterday, last month), the Simple Past Tense is almost always the correct choice in SSC fill-in-the-blank questions.

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The disclaimer read that no animals were harmed (1)________ the filming of that scene. However, they forgot that the brand of lipstick that was applied (2)________ the heroines lips for that scene was manufactured from crushed cochineal bugs, which release a pigment commonly used in red lipstick. The other items in the film studio (3)________ used animal fats during their manufacturing. The actors who (4)________ that they are vegan in past interviews are unaware of their indirect involvement in such acts of cruelty against animals. The indirect cruelty against animals does not stop here. For example, the extensive disposal of plastic waste in oceans has made plastic a part of the animal food chain, which is detrimental (5)________ our entire ecosystem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires the preposition that correctly follows the adjective "detrimental". The standard fixed collocation is "detrimental to", meaning causing harm or damage to something.

• Rule — Fixed preposition with adjectives: Several adjectives in English are always followed by a specific preposition; "detrimental" is always followed by "to" (never "on," "in," or "for").

• Applying the rule: the extensive disposal of plastic waste... is detrimental to our entire ecosystem.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "on" is incorrect; it does not form part of the standard fixed collocation with "detrimental."

• Option 3: "in" is incorrect for the same reason — it is not the preposition conventionally paired with "detrimental."

• Option 4: "for" is incorrect; it does not fit the fixed adjective-preposition pairing tested here.

NOTE

• Other adjective + fixed preposition combinations frequently tested in SSC: beneficial to, harmful to, dangerous to, useful to/for, responsible for, capable of, afraid of.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the sentence.
She was asked by the elders to wear a skirt covering her knees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Exposing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "covering" in the sentence means to hide or protect something from view by placing something over it (ढकना). Its antonym is "Exposing", which means to uncover something and leave it visible, without protection (उघाड़ना / खुला छोड़ना).
◦ Example: Her torn sleeve was exposing her elbow.

• Applying the meaning: a skirt that covers the knees hides them from view, while a skirt exposing the knees would leave them visible — exactly the opposite sense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Expanding (फैलाना): To increase in size or extent — unrelated in meaning to "covering."

• Option 3: Expecting (आशा करना): To believe that something will happen, or to be pregnant — unrelated in meaning to "covering."

• Option 4: Expounding (विस्तार से समझाना): To explain a theory or idea in detail — unrelated in meaning to "covering."

NOTE

• The words "Expanding," "Expecting," and "Expounding" are commonly used as distractors in SSC vocabulary questions because they sound and look similar to each other (all begin with "Exp-"); always focus on the exact meaning, not just the spelling pattern.

• Other synonym-antonym pairs with "cover/expose": conceal ↔ reveal, hide ↔ disclose, shelter ↔ expose.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The company has to be able to compete globally.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Support.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "compete" means to strive against others in order to win or achieve something; to be a rival (प्रतिस्पर्धा करना). Its antonym here is "Support", meaning to help, back, or assist someone/something rather than oppose or rival it (समर्थन करना / सहयोग करना).
◦ Example: Instead of competing with the local farmers, the new policy aims to support them.

• Applying the meaning: while "compete" involves striving against others (rivalry), "support" involves helping for others (cooperation) — the two are opposite in spirit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Attack (हमला करना): To use force or aggressive words/actions against someone — actually closer in spirit to competing/opposing, not its opposite.

• Option 3: Pervert (विकृत करना): To distort something from its original meaning or purpose — unrelated to the sense of "compete."

• Option 4: Impede (बाधा डालना): To delay or block progress — this is also a form of hindering, similar to opposing, not an antonym of "compete."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "compete": rival, contend, vie, contest.

• Other antonyms of "compete" commonly accepted in SSC: cooperate, collaborate, assist, help, support.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pronounciation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word is "Pronunciation", not "Pronounciation" — meaning the way in which a word is spoken (उच्चारण).
◦ Example: Her pronunciation of French words was flawless.

• Spelling key: the noun "pronunciation" drops the "o" that appears in the verb "pronounce"; it is spelt PRO + NUN + CI + A + TION, not "pro-noun-ciation."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Dissociation" — correctly spelt; means the act of separating or disconnecting from something.

• Option 2: "Clandestine" — correctly spelt; means done secretively, especially because illicit.

• Option 4: "Denunciation" — correctly spelt; means public condemnation of someone or something.

NOTE

• Other words where the noun form drops a letter present in the related verb: pronounce → pronunciation, describe → description, maintain → maintenance.

• Frequently tested tricky spellings in SSC: occurrence, questionnaire, embarrass, harass, liaison, entrepreneur, rendezvous.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
There was enough room in the spacious flat for all of our furniture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. roomy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "spacious" means having ample space; large in extent or area (विशाल / खुला-खुला). Its closest synonym among the options is "roomy", which also means having plenty of room; spacious (खुली जगह वाला).
◦ Example: The old house had a roomy kitchen where the whole family could gather.

• Both "spacious" and "roomy" describe a place with sufficient or generous space, unlike the other options, which describe places with little or restricted space.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Tiny (बहुत छोटा): Very small in size — nearly opposite in meaning to "spacious."

• Option 2: Cozy (आरामदायक): Warm, comfortable, and snug, often implying a small, intimate space — not the same as "spacious," which emphasizes largeness.

• Option 4: Cramped (तंग): Having too little space; uncomfortably small — the opposite of "spacious."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "spacious": capacious, expansive, sizable, ample.

• Other antonyms of "spacious": cramped, confined, cluttered, narrow.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
The army advanced into enemy territory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Retreated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "advanced" here means moved forward, especially in a military sense (आगे बढ़ना). Its antonym is "Retreated", meaning moved back or withdrew, especially from a difficult or dangerous situation (पीछे हटना).
◦ Example: Facing heavy losses, the army retreated to its base camp.

• Applying the meaning: an army that advances moves forward into territory, while an army that retreats moves backward, away from it — directly opposite actions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Protruded (उभरना): To stick out or project from a surface — unrelated to forward/backward movement of an army.

• Option 3: Arose (उत्पन्न होना): To come into existence or begin — unrelated in meaning to "advanced."

• Option 4: Commuted (आवागमन करना): To travel regularly between two places, typically for work — unrelated in meaning to "advanced."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "advance" (verb): progress, proceed, move forward.

• Other antonyms of "advance": withdraw, retire, regress, recede.

question: Which of the following sentences contains the ANTONYM of the word 'important'?
option_1: You always make me do all the trivial stuff.
option_2: Choose the right colour to make your bike stand out!
option_3: Namita also makes some very salient points in her newly revised preface.
option_4: I have some urgent questions for you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. You always make me do all the trivial stuff.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "important" means of great significance or value; deserving serious attention (महत्वपूर्ण). Its antonym is "trivial", meaning of little value or importance; insignificant (तुच्छ / मामूली), which appears in Option 1.
◦ Example: Don't waste your time on such trivial matters.

• Applying the meaning: the sentence "You always make me do all the trivial stuff" uses "trivial" to describe tasks of little importance — the exact opposite of "important."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: contains no word that is an antonym of "important"; "stand out" actually implies drawing attention/importance.

• Option 3: contains the word "salient", which means prominent or important, a synonym (not an antonym) of "important."

• Option 4: contains the word "urgent", which means requiring immediate attention, closely related to "important" in sense, not its opposite.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "important": significant, salient, crucial, vital, momentous.

• Other antonyms of "important": trivial, insignificant, trifling, negligible, petty.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence.
If it is sunny tomorrow, we go for a picnic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will go.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a conditional (if-clause) sentence referring to a probable future situation ("tomorrow"), which requires the First Conditional structure.

• Rule — First Conditional (Type 1):
◦ Structure: If + Subject + Simple Present, Subject + will + V1
◦ Used for real/probable situations in the future and their likely results.

• Applying the rule: If it is (simple present) sunny tomorrow, we will go (will + V1) for a picnic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "will going" is incorrect; "will" must be followed by the base form (V1) of the verb, not the "-ing" form.

• Option 2: "will went" is incorrect; "will" is never followed by the past form (V2) of the verb.

• Option 4: "goes" is incorrect; the simple present "goes" does not correctly express the future result required by the first conditional structure.

NOTE

• In the if-clause of a first conditional sentence, the verb is always in the Simple Present Tense, even though the meaning is future; the future tense with "will" appears only in the main/result clause.

• Other conditional types: Zero Conditional (If + present, present — general truths), Second Conditional (If + past, would + V1 — unreal present/future), Third Conditional (If + past perfect, would have + V3 — unreal past).

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence.
I am in a hurry so I will see you tomorow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. tomorrow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word is "tomorrow" — meaning the day after today (कल - आने वाला दिन).
◦ Example: I will submit my assignment tomorrow morning.

• Spelling key: tomorrow has a single "o" after "t", a double "r", and a single "o" before the final "w" — it is spelt TO + MOR + ROW.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "tomoorow" — incorrect; has a wrongly doubled "o" in the middle and only a single "r".

• Option 3: "toomorow" — incorrect; has a wrongly doubled "o" at the start and only a single "r".

• Option 4: "tomoorrow" — incorrect; has a wrongly doubled "o" in the middle, even though the double "r" is correctly placed.

NOTE

• Memory trick: think of it as "to + morrow" (an archaic word for "the next day"), which naturally gives the double "r".

• Other commonly misspelt everyday words in SSC exams: address, occasion, necessary, separate, embarrass.

question:
Read the given sentence carefully. Change meaning of the sentence by replacing the underlined word with its ANTONYM from the following options.
William Shakespeare is considered to be the most celebrated dramatist in the world of literature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. inglorious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "celebrated" means famous, widely admired and honoured (प्रसिद्ध / यशस्वी). Its antonym is "inglorious", meaning not bringing fame, honour, or glory; shameful or obscure (अपयशी / कुख्यात).
◦ Example: The team suffered an inglorious defeat in the final match.

• Applying the meaning: a "celebrated" dramatist is widely honoured and famous, while something "inglorious" lacks honour or fame — directly opposite senses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Laureate (सम्मानित/पुरस्कृत): A person honoured with an award for outstanding achievement — a synonym, not antonym, of "celebrated."

• Option 2: Acclaimed (प्रशंसित): Praised enthusiastically and publicly — a synonym of "celebrated."

• Option 4: Illustrious (प्रख्यात): Well-known, respected, and admired for past achievements — a synonym of "celebrated."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "celebrated": renowned, eminent, distinguished, famed, noted.

• Other antonyms of "celebrated": obscure, unknown, undistinguished, infamous (note: infamous means famous for something bad).

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.
It is my custom to get up early in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. habit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "custom" should be replaced with "habit". A "custom" (रिवाज़/प्रथा) refers to a traditional practice followed by a community, society, or culture, whereas a "habit" (आदत) refers to a settled, regularly repeated practice of an individual.
◦ Example: It is my habit to get up early in the morning, though it is not the custom in my family.

• Since the sentence describes a personal, regularly repeated action ("to get up early in the morning") of a single individual ("my"), the appropriate word is "habit", not "custom," which applies to a shared social/cultural practice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Addiction (लत): A compulsive, often harmful dependency on a substance or activity — too strong and negative a word for a simple daily routine like waking up early.

• Option 2: Perfection (पूर्णता): The state of being flawless or complete — unrelated to a repeated personal practice.

• Option 3: Oddity (विचित्रता): Something strange or unusual — does not fit the neutral, ordinary sense of a daily routine.

NOTE

• Commonly confused pair: "custom" (a practice of a group/society, often traditional) vs. "habit" (a practice of an individual, often unconscious/automatic).

• Related word: "convention" — an accepted social practice, similar to "custom" but broader.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The teacher asked the students to ________ attention towards the instructions given for the project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. pay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb that forms the correct fixed collocation with the noun "attention". In English, we always "pay attention" (ध्यान देना) to something, never "make," "keen/keep," or "have" attention.
◦ Example: Please pay attention to the safety instructions before the demonstration begins.

• Rule — Fixed collocations with nouns: Certain verbs are conventionally paired with specific nouns and cannot be freely substituted; "pay" is the verb that idiomatically collocates with "attention".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "make" is incorrect; "make attention" is not a standard English collocation.

• Option 2: "keen" is incorrect; "keen" is an adjective (meaning eager/sharp), not a verb, and cannot grammatically precede the noun "attention" in this blank.

• Option 3: "had" is incorrect; while "have/had" can precede some nouns, "had attention" is not the correct fixed collocation for this context.

NOTE

• Other common fixed verb-noun collocations tested in SSC: pay attention, make a decision, keep a promise, make an effort, take care, have a look.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
A gift from my teacher on the eve of the new year was a complete surprise.
option_1: like a cat on hot bricks
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a bolt from the blue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a bolt from the blue" means a sudden and completely unexpected event or piece of news (एकदम अप्रत्याशित घटना), matching the underlined phrase "a complete surprise" in the sentence.
◦ Example: His resignation came as a bolt from the blue to the entire office.

• The expression originates from the idea of a lightning bolt striking suddenly out of a clear blue sky — with no warning at all, just like an unexpected surprise.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Like a cat on hot bricks" (बहुत बेचैन/घबराया हुआ): To be extremely restless, nervous, or anxious — unrelated to the idea of a surprise.

• Option 3: "Like striking one's colours" (हार मान लेना/आत्मसमर्पण करना): To surrender or give up a struggle — unrelated to the idea of a surprise.

• Option 4: "Spilling of beans" (राज़ खोलना): To reveal a secret, often unintentionally — related to disclosure, not to the suddenness of a surprise.

NOTE

• Other idioms of suddenness/surprise: "out of the blue," "take by storm," "catch someone off guard."

• Do not confuse "a bolt from the blue" (unexpected event) with "once in a blue moon" (a rare occurrence).

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined phrase in the following sentence.
Even though she’s a celebrity, she doesn't draw any attention towards herself .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. keeps a low profile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "keeps a low profile" means to avoid attracting attention to oneself; to behave in a modest, unassuming way (ध्यान आकर्षित न करना / सादगी से रहना), matching the underlined phrase "doesn't draw any attention towards herself".
◦ Example: After the scandal, the actor kept a low profile for several months.

• Applying the meaning: even though she is a celebrity (who would normally attract public attention), she deliberately avoids it — this is precisely what "keeping a low profile" describes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "is hard to come by" (मुश्किल से मिलना): Describes something rare or difficult to obtain — unrelated to avoiding attention.

• Option 3: "keeps hot under the collar": The correct idiom is actually "hot under the collar" (गुस्से में होना), meaning to be angry or irritated — unrelated to avoiding attention.

• Option 4: "keeps up with the Joneses" (दूसरों की बराबरी करना): Means to try to match the social/material status of one's neighbours or peers — unrelated to avoiding attention.

NOTE

• Related idioms of modesty/attention: "stay in the background," "shy away from the limelight," "keep oneself to oneself."

• Related idioms tested with "collar": "hot under the collar" (angry), "a white-collar job" (office job).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
There is an old rivalry between the three families for ages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. among the three families.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "between the three families" contains an error in the choice of preposition. Since the sentence refers to more than two (three) families, the correct preposition is "among", not "between."

• Rule — Between vs. Among: "Between" is used when referring to exactly two people/things, while "among" is used when referring to more than two.

• Applying the rule: There is an old rivalry among the three families (three = more than two) for ages.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "of the three families" is incorrect; "of" does not correctly express the sense of a rivalry existing between/among multiple parties.

• Option 2: "No substitution required" is incorrect because the original sentence does contain an error — "between" is wrongly used for three families.

• Option 4: "in the three families" is incorrect; "in" would suggest the rivalry exists inside each family individually, not as a rivalry involving all three together.

NOTE

• Memory trick: "between" — think of "tween" as related to "two"; use it strictly for two entities. Use "among" for three or more.

• Similarly confused pair: "each other" (for two) vs. "one another" (for more than two).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word
Abundance
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Scarcity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Abundance" means a very large quantity of something; plentifulness (प्रचुरता / बहुतायत). Its antonym is "Scarcity", meaning an insufficient supply or shortage of something (कमी / अभाव).
◦ Example: The region faced a severe scarcity of clean drinking water.

• Applying the meaning: "abundance" denotes more than enough of something, while "scarcity" denotes not enough of it — directly opposite quantities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Fortune (भाग्य/धन): Wealth or luck — unrelated in meaning to the quantity sense of "abundance."

• Option 2: Excitement (उत्तेजना): A feeling of enthusiasm or eagerness — unrelated in meaning to "abundance."

• Option 4: Prosperity (समृद्धि): The state of being successful and having plenty of money/resources — actually a near-synonym of abundance (a state of plenty), not its opposite.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "abundance": plenty, profusion, affluence, wealth.

• Other antonyms of "abundance": scarcity, dearth, shortage, paucity, deficiency.

question:
Identify the most appropriate synonym of the following word.
Sceptical
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Incredulous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Sceptical" means having doubts or reservations about something; not easily convinced (संदेहशील). Its closest synonym among the options is "Incredulous", which also means unwilling or unable to believe something; showing disbelief (अविश्वासी).
◦ Example: She gave an incredulous look when he claimed to have finished the marathon in two hours.

• Both "sceptical" and "incredulous" describe an attitude of doubt or disbelief toward a claim or statement.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Stoic (अविचल/धैर्यवान): Enduring hardship without showing feelings or complaint — unrelated to doubt or belief.

• Option 3: Garrulous (बातूनी): Excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters — unrelated to "sceptical."

• Option 4: Insensitive (असंवेदनशील): Lacking sympathy or awareness of others' feelings — unrelated to "sceptical."

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "sceptical": doubtful, dubious, distrustful, suspicious, cynical.

• Other antonyms of "sceptical": convinced, credulous, trusting, certain.
